title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sectoral Support of IDPs transferring to alternative sites and resumption of school activities in Sheraro Wereda of Northwest Zone of Tigray Region.

description.narrative:
ltpgtThis integrated multi-sectoral support of IDPs including persons with disabilities transferring from schools to alternative sites and resumption of school activities in Shiraro district of Northwest zone of Tigray region. The project will be implemented by Imagine1day lead consortium including three national NGOs namely, ltspangtAction for Social Development and Environmental Protection Organizationltbgt (lt/bgtlt/spangtASDEPO), NEXUS Ethiopia and Development Expertise Center (DEC) for ten months. The consortium members are selected considering their sector expertise and operation presence in the project targeted districts. ltbrgtlt/pgt
ltpgtDEC will implement the Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) component with a focus on decommissioning of communal infrastructure and environmental mitigation, assisting and protect IDPs before and during movement, promoting protection and dignity, and providing CCCM capacity building support to benefit 15,868 IDPs including people with disabilities aiming to enhance the well-being and protection of displaced individuals through CCCM interventions.ltbrgtltspangtltbrgtImagine1day will lead the consortium and also implement the Education and Protection interventions. lt/spangtltspangtThe lt/spangtltspangt focuslt/spangtltspangt of the education intervention will be lt/spangtltspangton engaging schools in life-saving education interventions, strengthening the capacity of education institutions, and providing quality education for crisis-affected children. This project contributes to these objectives by conducting blt/spangtltspangtack to school lt/spangtltspangtcampaignslt/spangtltspangt and lt/spangtltspangt awareness raising for out of school children and caregivers,lt/spangtltspangt repair and maintenance of schools previously occupied by IDPs, provision of teaching and learning materials, lt/spangtltspangtsafeguarding learning environments, coordinating life-saving interventions, local lt/spangtltspangteducation system strengthening, lt/spangtltspangtand enhancing education access for 3,000 internally displaced children and host communities, including those with disabilities through basic repair, fixture, clean up,lt/spangtltspangt furniture provision andlt/spangtltspangt provision of scholastic materials for most vulnerable out of slt/spangtltspangtchlt/spangtltspangtool childrenlt/spangtltspangt.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe protection component to be implemented by Imagine1day encompass a multifaceted approach to enhancing the protection of 8,105 conflict-affected internally displaced individuals, including women, girls, men, and boys including people with disabilities, especially those transitioning from schools to alternative sites through various interventions such as CP /GBV case management, mental health and psychosocial support, multi-sectoral referral services, and public awareness campaigns on gender-based violence (GBV), and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).ltbrgt
ltbrgtlt/pgt
ltpgtNEXUS will implement the ESNFI component of this project with the aim to increase equitable, safe, and inclusive access to emergency shelter and household necessities while minimizing environmental impact and enhancing the protection and living conditions of crisis-affected people. The project will provide equitable access to adequate shelter solutions to safeguard health, security, privacy, and dignity for 3,733IDPs including persons with disabilities. lt/pgt
ltpgtlt/pgt
ltpgtASDEPO will implement the WASH component with the plan to benefit 14,038 IDPs including those with disabilities through strengthening of access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services, improvement of health and well-being for crisis-affected IDPs, upgrading non-functional water systems with gender-informed approaches, providing gender-responsive hygiene promotion activities, and rehabilitating inclusive sanitation facilities.ltbrgtltbrgt lt/pgt
ltpgtOverall, this integrated multi-sectoral support project will benefit 41,819 (most vulnerable conflict affected IDPs who are moved/transferred from the schools to alternate/return sites through education, protection, WASH, ESNFI, and CCCM interventions. Specifically, the project will directly benefit 17,741IDPs (4,540 women, 4,662 girls, 4,118 boys, 4,421men 2,118 PwDs) and 24,171 community members indirectly. lt/pgt
